extension.news: [B]1.3.1[/B][CR]- The weather icons are now higher resolution outline icons built into the skin, so the forecast is drawn from the skin's own set rather than Kodi's smaller default one.[CR]- If you prefer a different set you can still choose one under Settings, Skin Settings, and your choice still overrides the built-in icons exactly as before.[CR]- Nothing else changed, and nothing changes on any platform.[CR][CR][B]1.3.0[/B][CR]- The Siri remote fixes have moved out of this skin and into the Apple TV Fixes add-on, which is the same add-on that carries the Python repair and is in the same repository. If you are on an Apple TV, install it once and both fixes are yours whatever skin you use afterwards.[CR]- Apple TV owners already running it: update it to 1.1.0 and the remote keeps behaving exactly as it does now. Nothing else to do.[CR]- Apple TV owners NOT running it: your Siri remote goes back to Kodi's stock behaviour when you update this skin, which means back stops playback in fullscreen video and back at the home screen opens the Favourites window. Installing Apple TV Fixes puts it right again.[CR]- Why: a remote belongs to the box, not to a skin. Written from a skin it only worked while you used this skin, and it would have been written again by every other skin that copied the idea. This skin now runs no code of its own on any platform.[CR]- Nothing changes on Fire TV, Android, Windows, Linux or macOS. Nothing that draws on screen changed at all.[CR][CR][B]1.2.8[/B][CR]- The Apple TV Python fix is now a separate add-on that Apple TV users install themselves. It is called tvOS Python Fix and it is in the same repository as this skin. Install it before this skin, once, and you will not need to think about it again.[CR]- 1.2.7 installed it automatically as part of the skin. That put an Apple TV workaround on every Fire TV, Android, Windows, Linux and macOS box as well, where it does nothing.[CR]- If you are already on 1.2.7 and have it, updating to this release leaves it installed and working. Nothing is removed from your box.[CR]- Nothing changes on any other platform.[CR][CR][B]1.2.7[/B][CR]- Apple TV only: installing this skin on a brand new box no longer throws an error at you. Kodi installs a skin's dependencies before the skin itself, so POV was being installed and started before the skin that repaired Apple TV's Python was even on the box, and POV failed in front of you. The repair now ships as its own small add-on, tvOS Python Fix, and Kodi installs that one first.[CR]- Apple TV only: because the repair is no longer part of the skin, it now works for every add-on that fetches anything over the internet, whether or not this skin is the one you use. Multi Weather and EZ Maintenance++ included.[CR]- A NEW install now starts with four more settings already set the way this skin is meant to look. Media flags are off, so posters are not covered in codec and resolution badges. Ratings show as a score instead of nothing. Fanart backgrounds are off. Home rows show 10 items instead of 15.[CR]- All four are ordinary skin settings and every one of them is one click to change back, under Settings, Skin Settings: "Show media flags", "Choose rating to display for media items" and "Number of media items to show in home screen list" are under General, and "Show media fanart as background" is under Artwork.[CR]- EXISTING boxes are not touched. Any box that has already run 1.2.4 or later keeps every setting exactly as you left it, including the four above and the main menu you arranged. These defaults are applied once, on a profile that has never run this skin, and never again.[CR]- The home row size setting is renamed to "Number of media items to show in home screen list", because the number it holds counts films, episodes, albums and channels rather than the menu items beside it.[CR]- There is no 1.2.6. That number was built and tested but never released, and it is skipped rather than reused so that no two builds can ever share a version.[CR]- No change on Fire TV, Android or desktop. The Siri remote keymap is unchanged.[CR][CR][B]1.2.5[/B][CR]- A NEW install now starts with five main menu items: Movies, TV shows, TV, Add-ons and Weather. Music, Music videos, Radio, Pictures, Videos, Games and Favourites start switched off.[CR]- None of those seven are gone. Every one of them is still listed, and switching any of them back on is one click, under Settings, Skin Settings, Main menu items.[CR]- EXISTING boxes: if yours is updating from 1.2.4 the main menu you arranged is left exactly as it is and nothing changes. If yours is updating from 1.2.3 or earlier straight to this release, its main menu WILL be set to those same five items, because 1.2.4 is the release that marks a box as already arranged and yours never ran it. Switch the ones you want back on in Skin Settings.[CR][CR][B]1.2.4[/B][CR]- Skin settings no longer show rows that cannot do anything. Switch a home menu item off and its "Edit widgets" and "Default select action" rows now disappear instead of sitting there greyed out. Movies, TV shows, Music, Music videos, TV, Radio and Add-ons all behave this way.[CR]- Turn off "Show media fanart as background" and the three fanart pack pickers go with it. Turn off the video OSD autoclose and its seconds row goes too.[CR]- "Choose genre fanart pack" was worse than greyed out. With fanart switched off it stayed fully clickable and picking a pack did nothing at all. It now hides alongside the other two pickers.[CR]- The virtual keyboard suggests words as you type. Kodi installs the AutoCompletion add-on together with the skin, on an update as well as on a fresh install, so the suggestion strip above the keyboard is no longer permanently empty.[CR]- Groundwork with no visible effect: this release marks profiles that already run the skin as arranged by their owner, so that a later release can lay out a default home menu on brand new installs only, and can never rearrange a box that is already set up the way you want it.[CR][CR][B]1.2.3[/B][CR]- "Number of items to show in home screen lists" now applies to every home row. The Movies and TV shows poster rows already followed it. The Music, Music videos, Add-ons, Games, TV and Radio rows were fixed at 15 and no setting could move them.[CR]- The live TV and radio rows that carried no limit at all were rendering their whole directory instead of a row. On a Fire TV with the setting at 5, the TV channel groups row held all 12 groups while the poster rows held 5.[CR]- The random music video artists row was pinned to 10 and now follows the setting like the rest.[CR]- The Categories rows stay at 20 on purpose. They are navigation rather than content, so shrinking them would remove entries such as Playlists and Add-ons.[CR]- The setting takes effect without restarting Kodi, a few seconds after the row is next on screen.[CR][CR][B]1.2.2[/B][CR]- Apple TV only: POV, Multi Weather and EZ Maintenance++ work again. Kodi 22's Apple TV build ships a Python with a piece missing that every add-on fetching over the internet needs, so those add-ons failed the moment they started. The skin puts that piece back on every start, and puts it back again if an add-on update removes it.[CR]- Apple TV only: the Siri remote no longer opens the Favourites window when you back out of a video, and back in fullscreen returns to the menu with playback continuing instead of stopping it. Double play/pause goes back into fullscreen, and select opens the OSD on live TV.[CR]- No change on Fire TV, Android or desktop.[CR][CR][B]1.2.1[/B][CR]- POV is now a real install dependency, so Kodi pulls it in with the skin instead of leaving the Movies and TV shows rows empty on a box that does not have it.[CR]- Skin details rewritten to describe this skin rather than stock Estuary.[CR][CR][B]1.2.0[/B][CR]- Movies and TV shows home tabs are driven by POV rather than the local library, with per-row toggles in skin settings.[CR]- Main-menu items and search open POV directly.[CR]- Rounded poster treatment ported from Estuary 8.[CR]- Trimmed 1.9 MB of unreachable payload out of the package.
extension.summary: Estuary with the Movies and TV shows tabs driven by POV.
extension.description: Estuary POV is Kodi's stock Estuary with its Movies and TV shows home tabs rebuilt around the POV add-on instead of the local video library. Trending, popular, premieres, upcoming, in progress and watched rows all come from POV, each row can be switched off individually in skin settings, and the main-menu items and search open POV directly. Posters carry the rounded treatment from Estuary 8. Requires Kodi 22 (Piers) and the POV add-on.
extension.disclaimer: The Movies and TV shows tabs need the POV add-on. Kodi installs it with the skin.
